rejected: R8 arch tail with vertical fins and raised flat center roof
recommended_candidate: Two-surface inverted-V directly supported by twin booms; remove separate vertical fins and flat center roof

alternatives.judgment: Smallest architectural departure; separate pitch/yaw surfaces; silhouette can be improved with sweep and taper without bending into an arch
Requires a coherent center support arrangement for the existing twin booms; avoid unsupported center junction

sources.evidence: NASA explicitly describes rear engine, high wing, twin tailbooms and inverted V tail.
Designer documents pitch/yaw control mixing, combined deflection limits and longitudinal/lateral sizing with AVL; values are for FVA-30, not this aircraft.
Visual inspection shows connected inclined aft members between wing ends and aft body. Image does not provide dimensions, structural details or control architecture.

required_checks: horizontal and vertical projected area and tail moment arms
CG range and pitch/yaw trim/control authority
combined ruddervator travel and servo linkage
structural load path and removable joints
limitations: No aerodynamic superiority inferred from appearance or another aircraft. R8 tail is rejected and not promoted.
